newsitem.title: UK: London Clubs in "satisfactory" start to yr.
newsitem.headline: London Clubs in "satisfactory" start to yr.

text.p: Casino operator London Clubs International Plc on Tuesday reported a "satisfactory" start to the new financial year both in the UK and overseas.
"We are well positioned to take full advantage of the rapid expansion of gaming internationally," chairman Sir Timothy Kitson said in the results statement.

London Clubs, which operates seven casinos in London, earlier reported pretax profits of 35.3 million stg in the year to March 30, up from 33.3 million the year before. It announced a total dividend of 8.25 pence per share, up from 7.75 pence.

The company's Egyptian casinos saw "encouraging" trading in the year to March 30, while its UK operations had "especially strong trading" towards the end of the financial year, more than offsetting the quiet months of October and November.

The group said it has been granted a license for the new casino in London, to be known as "50 St James", subject to the surrender of the existing gaming licence for the Ritz Club when the lease of the present premises expires in June, 1998.
London Clubs continues to look to expansion overseas. In January the group entered into a letter of intent to invest $50 million for a 25 percent stake in the Aladdin casino in Las Vegas.
In February, the company announced a hostile all paper bid worth 190 million stg for rival casino Capital Corp Plc. This was referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) in April.
London Clubs, while "surprised" at the referral, said they have made detailed submissions to the MMC as part of the inquiry.
"We believe that there are no public interest issues which should prevent it from recommending to the Secretary of State for Trade and Industry that the bid should be cleared," it said.
The MMC has to make its recommendation to the Secretary of State by July 7, whose decision is expected by the beginning of August.
